Forecast Discussion

Low pressure moves from northern Maine to Nova Scotia today, and high pressure over the middle of the country keeps a cold northwest flow over the mountains. Snow showers taper to flurries along the western escarpment this morning. A flurry may linger there into early afternoon. Clouds decrease this afternoon.

High pressure builds in from the Midwest Sunday. Sunshine returns, and the afternoon is cold but less cold than today.

The high settles over the central Appalachians by Tuesday and stays for the rest of next week. Low pressure crosses the Gulf early in the week but stays far to our south. The weather next week will be as boring as it was exciting (at least for the western half of the Appalachians) this weekend--gradual warming and dry with sunshine galore.

Temperatures will be above average for the second half of next week. The next rain will wait until the week of Thanksgiving. Exactly when remains to be determined.
